what: Watts Water makes the valves, backflow preventers, drains and controls that sit inside plumbing and heating systems in buildings, and the electronic controls that manage them.
customers: Plumbing and heating contractors, buying through wholesalers, for both new buildings and repairs.
money: Asia Pacific, Middle East and Africa
the same products in other regions
moat: Products written into plumbing codes and specified by engineers, sold through wholesalers that contractors visit daily: the specification is the barrier, not the product itself.
risks: Non-residential construction has been weak and sets much of the demand
27 times earnings for a business growing in the mid single digits
Copper and brass costs move the margin
opportunities: A 14.0% net margin and $370M of free cash flow, with $406M of cash against $289M of debt
Revenue grew from $1.8B to $2.4B in four years
Smart and connected water controls carry higher margins and are a growing share of the mix
watch: Organic sales growth and the operating margin, which has been rising.
